title: "Inverse-transform sampling"

The empirical Turkish interrogative-lemma PMF assigns probability to labels, while a computer's basic random-number generator produces values on the unit interval. **Inverse-transform sampling** maps those uniform values into draws from the target PMF.

## From cumulative mass to labels

For an ordered numerical support, define the generalized inverse CDF by

$$
F^{-1}(u)=\inf\{x:F(x)\geq u\},
\qquad 0<u<1.
$$

If $U\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)$, then $F^{-1}(U)$ has CDF $F$. For categorical labels, we first assign a computational order. That order does not imply that *hangi*, *kim*, and *ne* form a linguistic scale.

The construction works because, at continuity points of $F$,

$$
\mathbb{P}\!\left(F^{-1}(U)\leq x\right)
=\mathbb{P}\!\left(U\leq F(x)\right)
=F(x).
$$

```{r}
#| label: inverse-ud-questions
library(ggplot2)

questions <- read.csv(
  "data/ud-turkish-boun/question-core-arguments.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
counts <- as.data.frame(table(questions$lemma), responseName = "count")
names(counts)[1] <- "lemma"
counts$target_probability <- counts$count / sum(counts$count)
counts$lower <- c(0, head(cumsum(counts$target_probability), -1L))
counts$upper <- cumsum(counts$target_probability)

inverse_sample <- function(n, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  u <- runif(n)
  index <- findInterval(u, c(0, counts$upper), rightmost.closed = TRUE)
  index[index > nrow(counts)] <- nrow(counts)
  data.frame(draw = seq_len(n), u = u, lemma = counts$lemma[index])
}

diagnostic_n <- 10000L
diagnostic_seed <- 20261018L
draws <- inverse_sample(diagnostic_n, diagnostic_seed)
simulated <- as.data.frame(table(draws$lemma), responseName = "sampled_count")
names(simulated)[1] <- "lemma"
comparison <- merge(counts, simulated, by = "lemma")
comparison$sampled_probability <- comparison$sampled_count / diagnostic_n

stopifnot(
  nrow(questions) == 167L,
  abs(tail(counts$upper, 1) - 1) < 1e-12,
  all(draws$lemma %in% counts$lemma),
  sum(comparison$sampled_count) == diagnostic_n
)

comparison
```

The cumulative intervals $[c_{k-1},c_k)$ have widths

$$
c_k-c_{k-1}=\widehat p_k.
$$

Thus a uniform draw lands in the interval for lemma $k$ with the empirical lemma probability $\widehat p_k$.

```{r}
#| label: plot-inverse-ud-questions
#| fig-cap: "Empirical Turkish interrogative-lemma probabilities and proportions from an inverse-transform diagnostic."
plot_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(lemma = comparison$lemma,
             probability = comparison$target_probability,
             source = "empirical target"),
  data.frame(lemma = comparison$lemma,
             probability = comparison$sampled_probability,
             source = "inverse-transform diagnostic")
)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(lemma, probability, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.72), width = 0.65) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("empirical target" = "grey55",
                               "inverse-transform diagnostic" = "#8B1A1A")) +
  labs(x = "Interrogative lemma", y = "Probability", fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The simulation is an implementation check, not a replacement for the corpus probabilities. Increasing the number of draws generally reduces simulation error, while it does nothing to repair the corpus's sentence clustering or register coverage.

## Check your understanding

1. Inspect the first rows of `draws` and verify each interval assignment manually.
2. Change `diagnostic_n` and compare the absolute errors.
3. Reverse the category order and confirm that the target masses remain attached to the same labels.
4. Why are the simulated proportions not new linguistic observations?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The first six uniforms, 0.4051, 0.7612, 0.1691, 0.9279, 0.3046, and 0.3345, all fall in the *ne* interval $[0.119760,1]$, so each is assigned *ne*. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. With seed 20261018, increasing `diagnostic_n` from 10,000 to 100,000 reduces the *hangi*, *kim*, and *ne* errors from 0.001064, 0.002196, and 0.003260 to 0.000146, 0.000786, and 0.000640. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. Reversing category order changes interval locations but not widths, so the target masses remain 0.017964 for *hangi*, 0.101796 for *kim*, and 0.880240 for *ne*. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. The simulated proportions are computational draws from the empirical PMF, not newly observed Turkish tokens or annotations. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [random-seed page](random-seeds.qmd) separates reproducibility of the computation from replication of the linguistic data.
